quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 earnings deck (consolidated, KRW 100 million units): AI revenue KRW 59.1 billion (+71% YoY, 81% of revenue) - AI compute (data center) KRW 47.7 billion (+59%), AI memory KRW 5.0 billion (KRW 6.3 billion in Q1, nil a year earlier), on-device AI KRW 5.4 billion, physical AI KRW 1.0 billion; non-AI KRW 13.8 billion (-20%). Memory revenue KRW 16.0 billion (+176% YoY) vs non-memory KRW 56.9 billion (+29%); data-center revenue KRW 55.0 billion (+66%), smartphone KRW 14.6 billion. Q2 commentary: higher-spec socket demand from faster, higher-power AI accelerators, mass-production orders expanding beyond GPUs to server CPUs and ASICs and share gains at key customers; premium AP sockets and SLT socket orders for a WMCM-based flagship smartphone AP; a one-off rise in legacy-memory sales temporarily diluted the mix while HBM and SOCAMM2 test solutions ramp and share rises at the three global memory makers.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 AI revenue KRW 59.1 billion; AI compute KRW 47.7 billion; AI memory KRW 5.0 billion; memory KRW 16.0 billion; data center KRW 55.0 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity expansion plan in the Q2 2026 deck: annual socket capacity to rise in phases from 2 million units in 2026 to 2.7 million (2027E), 3.7 million (2028E) and up to 5 million (2029E), a 2.5x increase, with capex executed step by step in line with demand, customer approval and utilisation - expanding existing lines, process optimisation, manufacturing AI and dedicated mass-production lines for key customers to improve revenue visibility; the company expects the added capacity to contribute to results from 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: annual capacity 2 million units (2026) to up to 5 million (2029E), 2.5x

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 outlook in the deck: growing mass-production orders for AI GPU, CPU and ASIC sockets, share gains at major customers and a rising average selling price from higher-spec products; initial supply of sockets for a new ASIC to a North American hyperscaler customer; launch of a next-generation high-speed server connectivity socket (ISC LinkEdge, tentative name) supplied to a North American data-center infrastructure customer; higher Final Test and SLT revenue from a North American mobile customer's new flagship smartphone; growth in HBM and SOCAMM2 product revenue and equipment/materials revenue from a major customer's Yongin semiconductor cluster investment; improving legacy-memory prices. The company plans to disclose a mid- to long-term shareholder-return and growth plan in H2.
quarterly_data.figure: initial supply of new-ASIC sockets to a North American hyperscaler; LinkEdge socket shipping to a North American data-center infrastructure customer
